[Problem]{.card-kicker} **Holes** [CF 13E · Holes](https://codeforces.com/problemset/problem/13/E){rating="2700"}

Each hole points to exactly one place — "somewhere to the right, or off the end" — so the ball's route is a walk along a forest of right-going arrows and the naive `1 pos` answer costs $O(\text{route length})$, up to $O(n)$ a query. The catch that rules out a plain precompute is the `2` update: a single $p$ change rewrites an arrow and every route through it.

Block the holes like @sec-sqrt-a1. Inside one block, a ball may hop several times before it exits to the right, but **which hole it exits from and how many hops that took depends only on the arrows within the block** — and there are at most $B$ blocks to the right, so a query can leap block-to-block instead of hole-to-hole. Cache, per hole $i$: `nxt[i]` the first hole *outside* $i$'s block the ball reaches (or $> n$ if it escapes), `cnt[i]` the hops taken to get there, and `end[i]` the last hole visited inside the block. A query chains those summaries across blocks; only $O(n/B)$ of them are touched.

[Solved in full in @sec-sqrt-p2-holes.]{.card-link}

:::
